No, he should've not posted it here at all, since it's a movie that has
absolutely no relation to the primary topic of this newsgroup: the
Vampire card game. It wasn't produced by White Wolf. It doesn't share
any of the same characters, nor ideas, nor concepts. It doesn't draw
from the same mythos. It doesn't even have a vampire IN the movie.

Simply attaching "OFF TOPIC" to a post doesn't excuse it -- the question
can quite properly be asked "look, you KNEW it was wrong, why did you do
it anyway?"

>the guys here are or have been role palyers, and could be interested in that

Lord of the Rings is a classic fiction trilogy by Tolkien. Many RPGs
owe their existence to it and have drawn heavily from it. This is not
an RPG, nor has it drawn from LotR in any visible fashion.

>subject. I'm not personnaly, but I am interested in freedomof Xpression. Are

Isn't it interesting when people in the wrong choose to incorrectly hold
up "freedom of speech!" or the like as justification for their actions,
lacking no other reasonable defense?

Doesn't it seem to happen an awful lot?

Doesn't it make you want to just slap them and say "Sit DOWN! That has
no place here -- its intent was to prevent censorship by the government,
and this is neither censorship, nor does it involve the government."

>you the moderator here ? If so, it is plainly your right to decise what has
>or hasn't its place here, but I think that sometimes speaking about
>something else than vampires, but with people you came to know (netwise)
>through VTES can also be a nice thing. Not quite friendship, but something
>like a feeling of belonging to a community.

I think that posts like that are the primary reason "moderators" came
into being in the first place -- no matter how well-meaning the
individual in question, the fact remains that this is a group about
V:TES, and discussions in here should at least be REMOTELY related to
V:TES when they start out.

If his post had been about what people thought of H.P. Lovecraft's
writings, he could at least have justified it by noting that V:TES has
drawn from the Cthulhu Mythos in at least two cases: Dagon's Call and
Ublo-Satha. It could then have spawned a rather interesting discussion
that would have been somewhat related to V:TES.

I think that he would find a much better feeling of "community" for a
Lord of the Rings discussion over in rec.arts.movies, where I'm sure
it's going to be a hot topic for awhile. Or any of a number of more
appropriate newsgroups (rec.games.frp.*, for example).

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:
Orpheus wrote:
>
> Well, I know what is supposedly, but I was surprised to see this :
>
> > >Sombody has see The Lord of the Rings yet???
> > >Do you like it? ;)
> >
> > Suitable for rec.arts.movies, perhaps, but not here.
>
> Why is that ?

Because it's not a topic for discussion in rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad.

> Ok, he should have precised "off-topics",

No, he shouldn't have. That has nothing to do with proper netiquette.
Posting only on-topic is proper netiquette. You need to understand that
just because you see somebody do something once in a while doesn't make
that behavior correct.

> but I bet most of the guys here are or have been role palyers, and could
> be interested in that subject.

That's possible. And that was probably his logic in the matter. But it's
irrelevant. Subscribing to this newsgroup does not indicate interest in
fantasy movies, however much crossover in interest there may exist between
the two subjects.

> I'm not personnaly, but I am interested in freedomof Xpression.

The problem is that one man's "freedom of expression" is another man's off-
topic noise, an irritation. The resolution between the two issues is to look
at what this tool, Usenet, is intended for and how it is intended to be used.
It was intended to all free of expression within only specific subjects which
are spelled out in the official newsgroup charter. That charter is agreed
upon when the newsgroup is formed. Although there may be a means of changing
newsgroup charters (I'm not sure of that issue), it hasn't been done, so the
expectation is that people post _on-topic_ in this forum, as spelled out in
the newsgroup charter. "Garou" can have his freedom of expression in the newsgroup
for which his post is topical. If one doesn't exist, he has the freedom to
propose one and discover if it has enough interest to be created. Otherwise,
what at question is not his freedom to express but his freedom to disrupt.

> Are you the moderator here ?

This is an unmoderated group, obviously. Had Derek been the moderator, he
either would not have permitted the post to be disseminated or he would not
object to the fact that it was disseminated since he would have had the power
to stop it.

The authority for topical content, whether a group is moderated or unmoderated,
is always the existing newsgroup charter. Sometimes people will vary in their
opinion of whether a given post is within the topics spelled out by the charter
but in this case, I don't think there's much question.

> If so, it is plainly your right to decise what has
> or hasn't its place here, but I think that sometimes speaking about
> something else than vampires, but with people you came to know (netwise)
> through VTES can also be a nice thing.

It can be a nice thing. But it is not a nice thing to do so here.

Fred

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:
Matt Latham wrote:
> As for the issue of off-topic posting, as far as I am concerned Jyhad
> players are a community, and as such if the person who posted the LotR movie
> question feels close enough to the people of this forum to want to discuss
> an item he thought would be of interest to the rest of the community then I
> don't have a problem with it. If I don't want to read it then I won't, but I
> sure won't waste forum space telling him not to do it.

You have a right to your opinion, as long as you understand that it isn't
really relevant at this time. Had you participated in the discussion which
led up to the vote that created this newsgroup, you could have contributed to
charter that got voted on. But I don't really see how you could interpret this
philosophy into a succinct statement that will tell people in advance whether
their post is off-topic or not.

What certain people (yourself included) may fail to understand is that the
topicality issue in newsgroups isn't something that's continually up for
discussion and reinterpretation on an ongoing basis. We can't "take a straw
vote" of the current regulars or something and decide to change the philosophy
of the group midstream. I suppose the current population of a newsgroup can
affect the content by what they choose to object and react to. And as you say,
if they don't want to loudly complain every time someone introduces some off-
topic thread that may have distinct crossover interest, then chances are the
practice will continue to some degree or another. Just be aware that your
lack of concern about it does not change the fact that it's (at least
technically) wrong and that others have a perfect right to complain and
request the practice cease if they find it to be a problem for them.

Fred

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:
Matt Latham wrote:
> When I read this newsgroup I read what interests me and ignore the rest. If
> other people did this instead of tearing people a new a**hole over things
> like off-topic posting and netiquette it would be a friendlier community by
> far.

I've already posted on this before. The choice people may have in terms of
selecting which articles they read is ignores the point that they have to
find it first. When a newsgroup is cluttered with a lot of off-topic threads
and a high noise to content ratio, that can get to be a challenge. The problem
with your philosophy is the slippery slope thing. It's not too bad right now
and it may never be a problem in this group. But it's not a bad thing to make
it clear that off-topic threads are at least not *supposed* to appear here lest
people get the idea that this newsgroup has no limits. It's much easier to
keep the problem in check then to fix it after it's gone bad.

As for tearing new holes in people, I agree that if people overreact to fairly
minor things - especially when it's just a newer poster who just didn't
understand the rules - that can be bad, too. Then newer posters and lurkers
start to get the idea that this is a mean, cold place full of highly irritable
people and it's better to keep your thoughts to yourself than to share them
lest you accidentally step on someone's toe. I hope everyone will contribute
to keeping these discussions as civil as possible.

Fred

>satisfy me plainly, I understand that everything cannot be discussed here, I

And here you AGAIN resort to hyperbole, completely mis-stating what I
said in an effort to produce a "bad guy" where there is none. If there
hadn't already been a long, detailed conversation in the past week about
off-topic posts, then I might have added some reasons. However, I
assumed that he has been reading the group and had already read that
discussion, so a brief suggestion of where that thread might be more
appropriate was suitable.

It is generally much better to step in and say "please, not here" at the
START of a thread, when people will read it and say "yeah, he's right,
not here" ... and not respond in the first place, as opposed to trying
to stop a thread once five or six responses have been posted to it
(where people will read and respond to something else before ever
reading the "please, not here" post).

I redirected followups for a very good reason -- generally, people who
post off-topic are relatively new to USENET, which is why they don't
understand why it's a bad idea to do so. Those same people generally
mash "reply" automatically, and so it's an excellent idea to make sure
that any replies go to a more appropriate location (since replies to the
thread will be off-topic as well, such as this one).

Reposted for completeness from Noal:

------------------------------------------------------------------

RFC1855 (a.k.a. FYI128):

Messages and articles should be brief and to the point. Don't wander
off-topic, don't ramble and don't send mail or post messages solely to
point out other people's errors in typing or spelling. These, more than
any other behavior, mark you as an immature beginner.

-------------------------------------------------------------------

Netiquette, by Virginia Shea:
http://www.albion.com/netiquette/rule10.html

If you do decide to inform someone of a mistake, point it out politely,
and preferably by private email rather than in public. Give people the
benefit of the doubt; assume they just don't know any better. And never
be arrogant or self-righteous about it. Just as it's a law of nature
that spelling flames always contain spelling errors, notes pointing out
netiquette violations are often examples of poor Netiquette.

_____________________________________________________

This seems pretty clear to me. Don't post off topic (as you want) AND don't
correct people in public, especially don't correct people in public in an
arrogant or self-righteous way.

Those are rules I can easily live with.

Matt
